subject: social-studies
title: Map a Community Region
objective: Use map features to describe a region and explain how people use local resources.

visual.title: Community region map
visual.caption: A simple map with a river, road, farm, town center, park, school, and compass rose.

teachingSupport.summary: Maps use symbols, labels, directions, and resources to explain how people use a place.
teachingSupport.description: Learners walk a floor map, match symbols to real places, and explain how a local resource supports the community.

diagramCallouts.title: Compass rose
diagramCallouts.body: Use north, south, east, and west to describe movement and location.

diagramCallouts.title: Map symbol
diagramCallouts.body: A simple picture stands for a real feature such as a school, river, road, or park.

diagramCallouts.title: Local resource
diagramCallouts.body: A resource is useful when people use it for water, food, travel, work, or recreation.

helperNotes: Point to the symbol, name the real place, then say why it matters.
Use direction words while physically walking the map.
Ask the learner to compare two places on the map before writing.

commonMisunderstandings.fix: Ask what real place each symbol stands for and how people use it.

commonMisunderstandings.mistake: Confusing a region with one single building.
commonMisunderstandings.fix: Have the learner describe land, water, weather, people, and resources together.

teachingSupport.confusionPrompt: Write whether you are stuck on directions, symbols, resources, or describing the whole region.

funTasks: Design a floor map with tape and walk from the school to the river using directions.
Trade resource cards and explain why a community might need each one.
Create a tour guide card for one region feature.
reward: Unlock the Community Cartographer badge after reading a new map.

sections.warmup: Look at a map symbol and guess what real place it represents.
sections.teach: Maps use symbols, labels, directions, and scale to show places. Regions can be described by land, water, weather, and how people live.
sections.guidedPractice: Find the compass rose, river, road, and town center on a community map.
sections.independentPractice: Write two sentences about how people use one local resource.
sections.activity: Build a community map and add three useful symbols.
sections.reteach: Start with one symbol at a time and connect it to the real place.
sections.challenge: Explain how the community would change if the river dried up.

quiz.prompt: What does a compass rose help you find?
quiz.explanation: A compass rose shows directions such as north, south, east, and west.

quiz.prompt: Which is an example of a local resource?
quiz.explanation: A river can be a resource when people use it for water, travel, or farming.

studentFacing.mission: Use the community map to explain how people move, live, and use resources.
studentFacing.whyItMatters: Maps help you understand real places, not just memorize symbols.
studentFacing.bigIdea: A region is described by features, directions, resources, and how people use them.
modelSteps: Find the compass rose and choose a direction.
Match each symbol to a real feature.
Explain how one resource helps people in the region.
studentFacing.example: A river can be a resource when people use it for water, farming, travel, or recreation.
studentFacing.nonExample: A school symbol is not just a picture; it stands for a real place in the community.
studentFacing.quickCheck: Point to a symbol, name the real place, then say why it matters.
studentFacing.studentSummary: Maps turn symbols and directions into a story about how a place works.
studentFacing.tutorHandoff: Tell the tutor if directions, symbols, resources, or describing the whole region feels stuck.

learningObjective: Use map features to describe a region and explain how people use local resources.
successCriteria: I can describe the big idea in Map a Community Region.
I can use a visual model or example to solve a new problem.
I can explain my reasoning and repair a misunderstanding.
I can retrieve and transfer the idea after a delay.
essentialQuestion: How can a map help us explain how people use a place?

knowledge: Maps use symbols, labels, directions, and resources to explain how people use a place.
capability: Use map features to describe a region and explain how people use local resources.
Use a model, example, or explanation to demonstrate the idea.
reasoning: Use evidence from the model or task to justify a choice.
retention: Retrieve the core idea after the original lesson context is removed.
transfer: Apply the idea to a new example, context, or problem.

phaseModules.title: Notice the challenge
phaseModules.studentAction: Look at the model and describe what you notice about Map a Community Region.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Use the community map to explain how people move, live, and use resources.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can say what I am trying to figure out before I choose an answer.

phaseModules.title: Build a model
phaseModules.studentAction: Maps use symbols, labels, directions, and scale to show places. Regions can be described by land, water, weather, and how people live.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Compass rose: Use north, south, east, and west to describe movement and location.
phaseModules.successCheck: My model shows the important parts and how they connect.

phaseModules.title: Spot the parts
phaseModules.studentAction: Sort the examples, evidence, or steps that belong to Map a Community Region.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Map symbol: A simple picture stands for a real feature such as a school, river, road, or park. Local resource: A resource is useful when people use it for water, food, travel, work, or recreation.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can explain why one choice fits and another choice does not.

phaseModules.title: Try the method
phaseModules.studentAction: Find the compass rose, river, road, and town center on a community map.
phaseModules.visualSupport: A river can be a resource when people use it for water, farming, travel, or recreation.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can use the model to complete a new example.

phaseModules.title: Explain the why
phaseModules.studentAction: Point to a symbol, name the real place, then say why it matters.
phaseModules.visualSupport: A school symbol is not just a picture; it stands for a real place in the community.
phaseModules.successCheck: My explanation names evidence or a rule, not only an answer.

phaseModules.title: Show your thinking
phaseModules.studentAction: Write two sentences about how people use one local resource.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Choose a drawing, spoken explanation, labeled model, or written response.
phaseModules.successCheck: Another learner could understand my reasoning from my proof.

phaseModules.title: Retrieve it later
phaseModules.studentAction: After a short delay, recall the key idea from Map a Community Region without copying the original example.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Maps turn symbols and directions into a story about how a place works.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can retrieve the idea when the order and example change.

phaseModules.title: Use it somewhere new
phaseModules.studentAction: Explain how the community would change if the river dried up.
phaseModules.visualSupport: A new context, example, or problem that keeps the same underlying idea.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can recognize when this idea is useful outside the original example.

phaseModules.title: Choose your next move
phaseModules.studentAction: Tell the tutor if directions, symbols, resources, or describing the whole region feels stuck.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Pick a helper note, alternate model, reteach path, or challenge path based on your evidence.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can name what is still confusing and choose a productive next step.

proofTasks.prompt: After a delay, retrieve the key idea from Map a Community Region.
Point to a symbol, name the real place, then say why it matters.
Write two sentences about how people use one local resource.
Complete a delayed Memory Vault check for Map a Community Region.
Explain how the community would change if the river dried up.

feedbackRules.hint: Ask what real place each symbol stands for and how people use it.
feedbackRules.action: Route to the alternate representation before retrying.

feedbackRules.result: Confusing a region with one single building.
feedbackRules.hint: Have the learner describe land, water, weather, people, and resources together.
feedbackRules.action: Route to the alternate representation before retrying.

reteachPaths.trigger: The learner misses the model or cannot explain the key relationship.
reteachPaths.action: Start with one symbol at a time and connect it to the real place.

prerequisiteRepairPaths.trigger: The learner cannot identify the basic parts needed for the lesson.
prerequisiteRepairPaths.action: Use a short sort, match, or vocabulary check before returning to the main task.

challengePaths.trigger: The learner completes the proof independently.
challengePaths.action: Explain how the community would change if the river dried up.

parentTeacherNotes: Treat independent transfer and delayed recall as stronger evidence than one immediate quiz score.
accessibilityNotes: Provide text, visual, oral, and keyboard-accessible ways to demonstrate understanding.
Do not rely on color alone.
